title: Cracking a weak hash
brief: The auth server stores passwords as MD5 hashes. Hash every word of the wordlist and see which one matches carlos.
hint.1: cat /etc/shadow.txt shows the hash of carlos. Compare it with others.
hint.2: hash -a md5 <word> prints the MD5 of a word. Try the words in /opt/wordlist.txt.
hint.3: One word produces exactly the hash in the file. Submit flag{word}.
walkthrough: Hash each wordlist word with hash -a md5 until one matches. It is sunshine.
debrief: Hashes are one-way, but common passwords are guessable by hashing a list. MD5 is fast, so attackers try billions per second. Defenders: use slow salted hashes (bcrypt, argon2) and long passphrases.
objective.hash: Hash candidate words with hash -a md5 <word>
